title: The first five minutes, out loud, before any code
takeaway: Restate, work an example, state the brute force, name the waste, propose and check: that is the part being scored.
sources: Steps 1 to 6 take five minutes and are the part being scored.
This is the step people skip, and it is the highest-value one.
This sentence is the hinge of the entire interview.
Every optimisation is the removal of a specific waste, and naming it is what turns "I remembered the answer" into "I derived the answer".

turns.text: Given an array of integers and a target, return the indices of the two numbers that add to the target.
So I am given an array of integers and a target, and I need to return the indices of the two numbers that add to the target. Is that right?
turns.note: Restating catches a misunderstanding while it is still free
One example by hand: the step people skip

turns.text: The brute force is a nested loop over every pair, which is O(n²) time and O(1) space.
turns.note: A correct baseline before a clever one

turns.text: The inner loop searches for target - nums[i] every time. That search is the expensive part.
turns.note: Naming the waste: the hinge of the interview

turns.text: I would store each value and its index in a hash map as I go. That is O(n) time and O(n) space. Does that sound reasonable to start with?
turns.note: Propose, then check before writing code
